# Linear transformations

So far, we have mostly talked about a single vector space. 
Now we move on to functions defined between distinct vector spaces.

We start with the following transformation in $\mathbb{R}^2$:

$$
👉\ \begin{pmatrix}
x' \\
y'
\end{pmatrix}=
\begin{pmatrix}
a && b \\
c && d
\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}
x \\
y
\end{pmatrix},\ \text{with}\ \begin{pmatrix}
a && b \\
c && d
\end{pmatrix}=
\begin{pmatrix}
2 && 1 \\
0 && 1
\end{pmatrix}
$$
